title: Team Recommendations Elite II fights
subject: The strongest *2 team for each of the 56 Elite legendary fights, with move bans and alternates

board.title: Team Recommendations Elite II fights — *2 teams with move bans

method.summary: For each of the 56 Elite legendary fights: the strongest *2 team for Elite II, every member's moves and the moves to ban, and who to bring instead — all Lv 100. Picked for Elite II: each team is the one that wins its fight most often at Elite II; where several win it as often, the one that also does best at Elite III. The ringed cell is Elite II; the other cells are the same six at the other tiers. Everything at *2: team, candidates and alternates are all at *2, Lv 100, not shiny (a rank is +15% on every stat; from *0, *2 takes 3 gems per Pokémon, 18 for a team). The best six from all 690 Pokémon of every rarity, one legendary at most (the game takes one per Elite fight). Search: the team search of the earlier boards at Elite II only, over the team and its moves together; then every place tries its replacements and its moves once more on 120 fights. Each search also starts from the team an earlier build's Teams board had for the same fight, and such a team stays unless the new one is clearly better on 1536 fresh fights (55 of the 56 teams are an earlier build's). Moves and bans: after each member, the moves it used at Elite II with the share of its turns (in 48 fights); in red after BAN, the moves to take away. New in v0.5.12: tap a learned move on a Pokémon's card and it no longer uses it in battle (it always keeps one attack); tap again to give it back. The ban lives on the Pokémon, not on the fight. 5 of the 56 teams have a ban (5 members). A ban has to earn its place: each was fought again, the team with it against the team without, on 384 fresh fights at Elite II, and is listed only if the team is clearly better with it (two standard errors, and 3 wins in 100); 1 ban was dropped, the 5 teams that kept one win 18 more fights in 100 with them. What these teams do at Elite II: 98 wins out of 100 on average (100 at Elite I); of the 56 bosses, 30 are beaten every time, 55 at least half the time. 43 teams put the boss to sleep with a status move. Wins are from seeded fights no search used: 384 for the team at Elite II, 192 at each other tier, 48 for an alternate. Fights that open only at night or at one moon phase run at the first hour they open; a fight without its own weather runs in clear weather.

algorithm.goal: Find the *2 team that wins each of the 56 Elite legendary fights most often at Elite II.
algorithm.engine: The game's own battle engine at build 824f567ed3
steps: Put everything at *2, Lv 100, not shiny; *0 to *2 costs 3 gems per Pokémon.
Search the best six from all 690 Pokémon of every rarity, at most one legendary.
Run the earlier boards' team search at Elite II only, over the team and its moves together.
Try every place's replacements and moves once more on 120 fights.
Also start from the earlier build's Teams board team; keep it unless the new one is clearly better on 1536 fresh fights.
Keep a ban only if the team is clearly better with it on 384 fresh Elite II fights (two standard errors and 3 wins in 100).
Score wins from seeded fights no search used: 384 at Elite II, 192 per other tier, 48 per alternate.

parameters.box: all 690 Pokémon of the four rarities

acceptance.pick: Most wins at Elite II; ties broken by Elite III.
acceptance.ban: A ban is kept only if the team is clearly better by two standard errors and 3 wins in 100 on 384 fresh fights.
acceptance.earlierTeam: An earlier build's team stays unless the new one is clearly better on 1536 fresh fights.

gameFacts: Everything is at *2, Lv 100, not shiny; a rank is +15% on every stat.
From *0 to *2 takes 3 gems per Pokémon, 18 per team.
At most one legendary per Elite fight.
A ban lives on the Pokémon, not on the fight; tapping a learned move removes it, tapping again restores it.
A Pokémon always keeps one attack.
A member left with only attacks the boss is immune to uses its status move every turn it can land (BAN N attacks, all but the ones it keeps).
Closed fights run at the first hour they open; no-weather fights run in clear weather.
5 of the 56 teams have a ban; 43 teams put the boss to sleep.
98 wins of 100 on average at Elite II; 30 bosses beaten every time, 55 at least half the time.

uncertain: The board lays the 56 cards in four columns: each region's cards flow from its header column into the next column (Kanto col 0→1, Johto 2→3, Hoenn 0→1, Sinnoh 2→3, Unova 0→1→2→3). The fight order here follows that flow, which differs from the earlier draft for Latias/Latios and Mesprit. Every boss name was read from its own header, so no card was placed by elimination.

Alternate rates: some cards print low rates as plain text instead of a plate (Kyogre among them). Every line the plate reader could not read, and every line where its two scale passes disagreed (40 lines), was read directly from the board crop. All 672 rates are integers 0-100; none is left null.
The I-V cells are read from each card's header band; `banGain` is stored for the 5 cards that print `BANS +N WINS AT ELITE II`.

A BAN marker belongs to the alternate, not to the slot: the board prints it on the first mention (Ninetales and Rotom (Heat) on Jirachi, for example) and lists the moves at the card's bottom. Every occurrence of that alternate in the card carries `withBan`, and the card-level list is in `alternateBans`.

An all-but ban line with no name under it applies to the member above it (Ho-Oh's Politoed, Meloetta Pirouette's Dusknoir). Every other all-but line is an alternate ban, stored in the board's wording ("14 attacks, all but Mud Shot, Earth Power").
